## 3. Current Security Posture

### 3.1 Network Security

#### 3.1.1 Network Architecture
[Describe and evaluate the current network architecture, segmentation, and zones]

#### 3.1.2 Perimeter Security
[Evaluate perimeter security controls including firewalls, IDS/IPS, and DMZ configuration]

#### 3.1.3 Internal Network Security
[Evaluate internal network security controls, including segmentation, monitoring, and traffic control]

#### 3.1.4 Wireless Network Security
[Evaluate wireless network security, including encryption, authentication, and guest access]

#### 3.1.5 Remote Access
[Evaluate remote access solutions, including VPN, MFA, and monitoring]

#### 3.1.6 Network Monitoring and Response
[Evaluate network monitoring capabilities, including logging, alerting, and incident response]

### 3.2 Endpoint Security

#### 3.2.1 Endpoint Protection
[Evaluate endpoint protection solutions, including antivirus, EDR, and application control]

#### 3.2.2 Patch Management
[Evaluate patch management processes for operating systems and applications]

#### 3.2.3 Configuration Management
[Evaluate system hardening and configuration management practices]

#### 3.2.4 Mobile Device Security
[Evaluate mobile device security, including MDM solutions and policies]

#### 3.2.5 Removable Media Controls
[Evaluate controls for removable media, including USB devices and external drives]

### 3.3 Access Control

#### 3.3.1 Identity Management
[Evaluate identity management practices, including provisioning, review, and deprovisioning]

#### 3.3.2 Authentication
[Evaluate authentication mechanisms, including password policies and MFA implementation]

#### 3.3.3 Authorization
[Evaluate authorization controls, including role-based access and least privilege principles]

#### 3.3.4 Privileged Access Management
[Evaluate privileged access management, including administrative account controls]

#### 3.3.5 Physical Access Controls
[Evaluate physical access controls to facilities, data centers, and sensitive areas]

### 3.4 Data Security

#### 3.4.1 Data Classification
[Evaluate data classification schemes and implementation]

#### 3.4.2 Data Protection
[Evaluate data protection mechanisms for data at rest, in transit, and in use]

#### 3.4.3 Data Loss Prevention
[Evaluate DLP solutions and their effectiveness]

#### 3.4.4 Encryption Management
[Evaluate encryption implementation and key management]

#### 3.4.5 Data Retention and Destruction
[Evaluate data retention policies and secure data destruction practices]

### 3.5 Cloud Security

#### 3.5.1 Cloud Service Provider Security
[Evaluate security of cloud service providers and shared responsibility model implementation]

#### 3.5.2 Cloud Configuration
[Evaluate cloud configuration, including identity management and access controls]

#### 3.5.3 Cloud Data Protection
[Evaluate data protection in cloud environments, including encryption and DLP]

#### 3.5.4 Cloud Monitoring and Logging
[Evaluate cloud monitoring, logging, and incident response capabilities]

### 3.6 Application Security

#### 3.6.1 Secure Development Practices
[Evaluate secure development lifecycle and practices]

#### 3.6.2 Application Vulnerabilities
[Evaluate common vulnerabilities in applications, including OWASP Top 10 issues]

#### 3.6.3 API Security
[Evaluate API security, including authentication, authorization, and input validation]

#### 3.6.4 Web Application Security
[Evaluate web application security, including authentication, session management, and input validation]

#### 3.6.5 Application Testing
[Evaluate application security testing practices, including SAST, DAST, and penetration testing]

## When to Use

Use throughout the project lifecycle to identify, assess, and track risks. This template is essential for projects with significant complexity, multiple stakeholders, or high business impact, where structured risk management provides decision-making value.

## When NOT to Use

Do not use for very low-risk, short-duration tasks where informal risk awareness is sufficient. Avoid this template if your governance framework requires a different risk management approach or if stakeholders prefer real-time risk dashboards over static registers.
